subject.title: Remote skill bin probe times out when node is co-located with gateway (macOS app as node on same host)

question: Should macOS app-backed nodes be probed immediately on connect, probed only after a stronger readiness/deferred backoff signal, or skipped only when co-located with the gateway?
rationale: Current main supports macOS `system.which` and `system.run`, but the remaining behavior crosses app-node readiness timing, co-location detection, retry/backoff policy, and the node exec contract.

options.title: Defer And Back Off Probes
options.body: Keep remote macOS skills supported, but delay initial app-node probes until readiness is stronger and add bounded retry/backoff for failed probes.

options.title: Skip Only Co-located App Nodes
options.body: Avoid probing loopback/co-located app nodes while preserving remote app-node probing for hosts that can execute skills.

options.title: Disable App-node Probing By Default
options.body: Stop automatic app-node remote skill eligibility unless users explicitly enable it, reducing warning spam at the cost of default remote skill support.

recommendation.title: Defer And Back Off Probes
recommendation.body: Keep remote macOS skills supported, but delay initial app-node probes until readiness is stronger and add bounded retry/backoff for failed probes.

likelyOwner.reason: The remote skill probe and node command-policy history makes this the strongest routing owner for the product-boundary choice.
